subject: Latency SLOs for Hosted API — draft targets and measurement windows
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Peter Jensen <peter.jensen@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Latency SLOs for Hosted API — draft targets and measurement windows

Hi Peter —

Following up from our call last week. Per Acme’s requirement for predictable latency, we put together a draft set of latency SLOs and a measurement approach for the Hosted API. These are intended to be enforceable operational commitments (SLO-based with credits) rather than aspirational performance numbers. High-level proposal: 

- Availability: 99.95% (monthly) for the Hosted API control plane and inference endpoints in US regions.
- Latency SLOs (for production text-generation/response calls, averaged by request type):
  - p50 <= 150 ms
  - p95 <= 800 ms
- Measurement window: rolling 30-day window, computed daily from our telemetry (per-route, per-region).
- Exclusions: planned maintenance windows (announced >=72h), force-majeure, and agreed burst-traffic surges (defined in proc doc).
- Remedies: Service Credits tiered by severity (example in attached SLA draft).

Notes and rationale: p50 is intentionally tight to reflect normal steady-state; p95 includes headroom for model cold starts & larger sequences. We can provide per-model profiles (we have different numbers for small vs. extra-large models) and route control if you want stricter SLAs on a per-model basis.

Attached: ACME_Redwood_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf (redlines and credit table), latency-metrics-sheet.xlsx (sample telemetry and how we compute percentiles).

If Acme wants a shorter measurement window (e.g., weekly) or a tighter p95 target, let me know — we can scope that as an exception request to Product/Infra and outline the mitigation plan (e.g., dedicated pool, reserved capacity).

Next steps: please confirm if the 30-day rolling window is acceptable or if you want us to propose a version with a 7-day window and tighter p95.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0132

Subject: Re: Latency SLOs for Hosted API — draft targets and measurement windows

Dylan —

Thanks for the quick turn. Acme appreciates the clarity. A few requests from our side before we move this into our legal/procurement queue: 

1) Can you tighten the p95 to 500 ms? That aligns with our internal SLAs for user-facing inference in the product (we're sensitive to tail latency).
2) We prefer a 7-day rolling window for p95 breaches so we can detect regressions faster and trigger mitigations (we can accept a longer window for availability).
3) How does this behave under bursts (our nightly batch + spikes)? We need to understand whether you treat short bursts as exceptions or count them against the SLO.

I attached Acme's standard SLA questionnaire (procurement redline). Also, please include a simple example of the credit calculation for a p95 miss across a 7-day vs 30-day window.

Appreciate if you can respond by EOD Friday — we have a partner exec review next Monday.

Best,
Peter Jensen
Head of Product Ops, Acme Analytics
peter.jensen@acme-analytics.com

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Latency SLOs for Hosted API — Acme wants p95 500ms / 7-day window — internal

Internal —

Peter asked for p95=500ms and a 7-day rolling window. He also asked how bursts are treated. Quick internal read:

- Product/Infra realities: our public Hosted API tails vary significantly by model and sequence length. For the median text generation model in US-east we can usually hit p95 ~450–700ms depending on sequence distribution. Guaranteeing 500ms p95 across all request types + regions without dedicated/reserved capacity is risky.
- Options to offer: 
  1) Scoped guarantee: p95 <= 600 ms on the Hosted API for US regions (7-day rolling), and 500 ms for a narrower SLA if Acme agrees to route production traffic through a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity).
  2) Hybrid approach: keep 30-day rolling window for standard Hosted SLA and offer a 7-day experimental SLA with limited credits for the first 3 months while we monitor.
  3) Exception language: For bursts (traffic > 3x baseline for > 30 mins) we treat that as an exception unless Acme pays for burst protection / reserved capacity.

Recommended: propose option (1) with p95=600ms for Hosted (7-day rolling) and a path to 500ms via Dedicated/reserved capacity. That gives Acme an operational improvement while protecting us from open-ended commitments. Also propose a canary period (30 days) with telemetry dashboard access; include the HubSpot link to the deal in the reply so CS/Product can add monitoring.

If you agree, I'll draft the customer-facing email and update the SLA PDF and credit table.

D

Subject: Re: Latency SLOs for Hosted API — final proposal and exception path

Hi Peter —

Thanks for the clear asks and the questionnaire. After internal review here's a customer-friendly proposal that balances Acme's tail-sensitivity with operational constraints: 

Final proposed commitments (Hosted API — US regions):
- Availability: 99.95% (monthly).
- Latency SLOs for production inference calls (per-route, per-region):
  - p50 <= 150 ms
  - p95 <= 600 ms (measured as a 7-day rolling window; computed daily)
- Burst / traffic surges: traffic >3x baseline for >30 minutes will be treated as an exception and excluded from SLO calculations unless Acme purchases burst protection or moves the traffic to a Dedicated pool.
- Path to 500 ms p95: available via Dedicated/reserved capacity SKU (we can provide pricing and a migration plan).
- Canary & monitoring: 30-day canary after sign-off during which credits are limited to a remediation-only posture (i.e., we will not apply automatic credits for the first 30 days while both teams validate telemetry).
- Remedies/credits: see attached SLA draft; example credit: 5% monthly service credit for each 0.2% point of unavailability beyond the SLA threshold. For latency misses, we propose an escalating credit table tied to magnitude and recurrence — detailed in the draft.

We updated the attached ACME_Redwood_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf and the latency-metrics-sheet.xlsx to show sample calculations for a 7-day vs 30-day window and a worked example of a p95 miss. Please review and let us know if Acme would like the Dedicated path (we can attach pricing).

If this structure works, we can send a redline-ready contract and loop in Legal/Procurement.

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
